scan_mode: Controls which search modes are used. "Quick" only scans the original audio files. It is fast and is the recommended first pass. "Long" only scans tempo and pitch variations of each file, helping identify songs that have been sped up, slowed down, or pitch shifted. For songs that have not yet had a "Quick" pass, the original file is included in the "Long" batch as well, so a fresh "Long only" session still scans everything. "Both" runs "Quick" to completion first, then "Long", which is a single click full scan at the cost of the longest run time. This setting is independent of the per song checkboxes in the Song Selection dialog, which decide which songs are candidates for each mode.
song_selection_help: The Song Selection dialog decides which songs are candidates for each mode. "Quick mode" scans the original audio file in every search mode you have enabled. "Long mode" scans tempo and pitch variations of the file, which is useful for songs that have been sped up, slowed down, or pitch shifted. For songs that have not yet had a "Quick" pass, the original file is included in the "Long" batch as well, so its original is scanned only once even though it is also part of a "Long" run. A song marked for both modes is handled inside the "Long" batch. This dialog is independent of the Scan Mode switch on the General tab. The dialog says which songs are candidates for each mode, while the Scan Mode switch says which modes actually run in this session.
pklz_folder_selection_help:
The PKLZ Selection dialog chooses which parts of the Audfprint Database Directory are used for Audfprint searches. You can tick whole folders or individual .pklz files, and ticking a folder covers everything inside it. If "Use full database" is checked, every PKLZ file is searched and the selection is ignored.

Because Audfprint can only be pointed at a folder, saving a selection physically moves the chosen .pklz files into a "___TEMP" folder inside your database, and the scan searches that folder. Anything you deselect is moved back out again, and checking "Use full database" moves everything back, so the files always end up either in their original place or in ___TEMP, never anywhere else. The moves happen when you press Save, and are repeated at the start of every scan so the staging folder always matches what you picked.

A selection of any shape is searched in a single pass, so unlike the old one-folder-per-run behaviour, Long Mode no longer has to regenerate its tempo and pitch variations once per selected folder.
negative_tempo_array: The tempo ratios (below 1.0) used to generate slowed-down/pitch-shifted-down variations of each file in Long mode. Edit this as a comma-separated list in brackets, e.g. [0.9, 0.95]. Leaving this empty uses only the positive array; leaving both empty restores the full default set of variations.
positive_tempo_array: The tempo ratios (above 1.0) used to generate sped-up/pitch-shifted-up variations of each file in Long mode. Edit this as a comma-separated list in brackets, e.g. [1.05, 1.1]. Leaving this empty uses only the negative array; leaving both empty restores the full default set of variations.
custom_webhook_name: Overrides the display name your Discord webhook uses when posting, replacing the default "WerZatSong".
custom_webhook_image: Overrides the avatar image your Discord webhook uses when posting. The link must start with either "https://cdn.discordapp.com/icons/", "https://cdn.discordapp.com/app-icons/" or "https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/", or Discord won't recognize it. The image must be in ".webp" format. You can get a correctly formatted link by setting the image as a Discord bot's profile picture and copying the link from there (if necessary, removing any size parameter at the end and, changing the extension to ".webp").
thread_count: Sets how many CPU threads Audfprint mode uses. Capped at 16 regardless of what you enter, to help prevent running out of memory. Leaving this unchecked allows Audfprint to use all available threads on your machine automatically.
musicbrainz_duration_range: Restricts MusicBrainz matches to songs whose duration (in seconds) falls between the two values you enter. Each value must be between 30 and 600; anything outside that range is reset to the default (30/600).
musicbrainz_extension: Helps MusicBrainz find a match when the beginning of your audio file is cut off or delayed by the number of seconds you enter. Must be between 1 and 25; anything outside that range is reset to the default (25).
audiotag_cooldown: Before every AudioTag request, WerZatSong waits a random number of seconds between the two values you enter here (default 10-30). This spreads requests out instead of hammering AudioTag's server back-to-back, which matters a lot on the free tier: the free plan is limited to roughly 1,000 identification requests per month, so unknown tracks can burn through that budget in as few as 100-200 files if run carelessly.
audiotag_rotate_after: After this many tracks have been processed with the current AudioTag key (default 100), WerZatSong takes the Pause Duration below, and, if "Use multiple AudioTag API keys" is enabled and another usable key is available, switches to it. This is a periodic safety checkpoint: it applies even with a single key, purely to avoid hammering AudioTag's server with a long uninterrupted run. Note the distinction between tracks and requests: a single track can involve one identification request plus several free status checks, so this counts tracks, not raw HTTP requests.
audiotag_pause_seconds: How long WerZatSong pauses (in seconds) once the "Pause after this many tracks" checkpoint is reached, before resuming (default 300 = 5 minutes). This applies whether or not multiple keys are configured.
audiotag_min_duration: AudioTag's server silently rejects very short clips with an "audio duration is too short" error in practice, even though the API itself only documents a 5-second floor. Any file shorter than the value you set here (default 15 seconds) is looped (repeating its own audio, not padded with silence) until it reaches this length before being sent to AudioTag, so short clips still get identified instead of being skipped.
audiotag_multi_key: When enabled, AudioTag searches rotate through the list of API keys below (each from a separate free AudioTag account) instead of using only the single AudioTag API Key from the .env section. Keys are tracked here in "assets/audiotag_keys.json": WerZatSong automatically marks a key exhausted or invalid based on the AudioTag server's own responses and moves on to the next usable one. This does not remove AudioTag's rate limits, and it does not replace the cooldown/pause settings above: using several keys still means hitting AudioTag's server more overall, so keep the cooldown reasonable and be considerate of their service.
search_depth: Controls how aggressively the program searches for a match (1-8). Higher values perform a more thorough "deep search" for low-quality clips, but may significantly increase processing time. The default is 4.
theme_mode: Changes the visual appearance of the application. Set to Light, Dark, or System Default to automatically match your OS settings.
language: Selects the language used for the interface. Changes take effect immediately.
python_command: Choose whether WerZatSong should be launched using the plain "python" command or the full path to the Python executable. Use the full path if you have multiple Python installations or if Python is not in your system PATH.
ffmpeg_command: Choose whether to use the plain "ffmpeg" command or the full path to the FFmpeg executable. Use the full path if FFmpeg is not in your PATH or if you need to force a specific version.
node_command: Choose whether to use the plain "node" command or the full path to the Node.js executable. Use the full path if Node is not in your PATH or if you have multiple versions installed.
hash_tables_dir: The folder where hash counts are saved (created automatically if missing). Hash counts are the plain-text files generated for each .pklz added to the database when "Create hash counts for each .pklz file added" is enabled: they show every audio file contained in a .pklz and how many hashes each one contributed. Use "Browse..." to pick a folder or type its path directly. If the field is left empty, it reverts to the default "hash_tables" folder next to the app.
console_logs_dir: The folder where console log dumps produced by "Print console output to log file" are saved (created automatically if missing). Use "Browse..." to pick a folder or type its path directly. If the field is left empty, it reverts to the default "console_logs" folder next to the app.
print_console_to_log: Writes everything currently shown in the Console to a timestamped .txt file inside the Console Logs Directory. The filename follows the pattern YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS_v{version}_WZSGUI_CLog.txt, so successive dumps never overwrite each other. Useful for attaching logs to a bug report or for keeping a record of a scan.
create_hash_tables_explanation: When enabled, every .pklz file added to the database via "Add pklz files..." will also have a hash count created for it. A hash count is a plain-text file showing every audio file contained in the .pklz and how many hashes each one contributed. Hash counts are saved to the configured Hash Counts Directory, preserving the original folder hierarchy.
